feedback.problem:
Consider the straight line with the parametric equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-2t \\ y=-5t \\ z=1-t\end{aligned}
$$

for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Find the Cartesian equation of this line.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3-2t \\ -5t \\ 1-t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2t \\ -5t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -5 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

This implies that the given line passes through the point $P(3,0,1)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨-2,-5,-1⟩.$ So, its Cartesian (canonical) equation is given by

$$
\frac{x-3}{-2}=\frac{y-0}{-5}=\frac{z-1}{-1}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Simplifying, we reach

$$
\frac{x-3}{-2}=\frac{y}{-5}=\frac{z-1}{-1}.
$$
